need: prepare a firmware upgrade for the edge firewall
clues: the upgrade could leave the VPN unusable for remote staff
the firewall must be back in its current state within minutes if anything goes wrong
the steps to return to the old firmware must be written down before work starts
appliesWhen: a change may fail and the team must be able to return the system to its previous state
explanation: A backout plan is a documented procedure, written before the change, that reverts a change that harms security or operations. It keeps a failed change from causing a long outage or leaving systems exposed.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: decide whether to move the payroll database to a new server
clues: no one has checked which systems and users the move would affect
the change board wants to know the security risks before it votes
the payroll application exchanges data with three other services
appliesWhen: the effects and risks of a proposed change must be understood before it is approved
explanation: An impact analysis assesses how a proposed change could affect systems, users, and security before it is approved. It finds risks early so they can be addressed or the change can be rejected.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: schedule a patch that takes the customer web portal offline
clues: customers use the portal heavily during business hours
traffic drops sharply late in the evening
the patch needs the portal service to restart
appliesWhen: a change causes downtime and must happen when it affects the fewest users
explanation: A maintenance window is a planned time frame for changes, chosen when use is lowest so that downtime affects as few people as possible.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: change the routing configuration of the core router
clues: the change affects every branch office
company policy says no production change may start without formal sign-off
the request is documented with its risks and a rollback plan

answer.item: Approval from the change advisory board (CAB)

appliesWhen: a production change needs formal review and sign-off before it starts
explanation: The change advisory board (CAB) evaluates, prioritizes, and approves or rejects proposed changes. Its approval process makes sure a change fits the organization's goals and does not add security risk before work begins.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: roll out a new endpoint security agent to every workstation
clues: a pilot group of twenty machines has run the agent for a week
the change board asked for evidence that the agent does not break business applications
nobody has reviewed what happened on the pilot machines yet
appliesWhen: the team must show that a change works as intended before it is deployed
explanation: Test results show whether a change or new security measure works as intended and does not cause new problems. Reviewing them before deployment gives the evidence the approval process needs.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: make sure every engineer applies the monthly server patches the same way
clues: two engineers patched the same server type in a different order last month
one engineer missed a step that left a service disabled
new staff join the operations team often
appliesWhen: a routine task must be done the same way every time
explanation: A standard operating procedure (SOP) is a step-by-step instruction set for a routine task. It keeps the work consistent and secure no matter who does it.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: find out who is accountable for a change to the customer database
clues: the change request names no responsible person
two departments each assume the other will check the security settings
auditors require one named person for each change

answer.item: Assigning an owner to the change

appliesWhen: a change needs one person who is accountable for carrying it out
explanation: Ownership names the person or team responsible and accountable for a change or an asset. Without an owner, tasks such as checking security settings can fall between teams.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: plan a migration to a new email platform
clues: the sales team depends on email to reach customers
the legal department must keep a record of all messages
the help desk will get many calls if users are not told in advance
appliesWhen: the groups affected by a change must be identified and involved
explanation: Stakeholders are the people and groups who are affected by a change or who can affect it. Involving them early surfaces their requirements, such as legal record keeping, and avoids surprises.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: recover from a failed release of the online ordering application
clues: the release ran a database migration that removed an old column
the previous version of the application cannot run against the changed database
the change policy allows a tested corrective release in this situation

answer.item: Failing forward with a corrective release

appliesWhen: a failed change cannot be safely reversed and a tested fix is deployed instead
explanation: Failing forward (also called fixing forward or rolling forward) recovers from a failed change by deploying a new corrective change instead of returning to the previous version. It is used when a rollback is impossible or riskier, for example after a data change the old version cannot handle, and the plan should be documented and tested before deployment.
source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Operational Excellence Pillar – OPS06-BP01 Plan for unsuccessful changes; xMatters – After a deployment error, should you fix forward or roll back?

need: stop unapproved software from running on the finance workstations
clues: new malware variants appear every day
the finance team uses only five approved applications
naming every harmful program in advance is impossible
appliesWhen: only approved applications may run and everything else must be blocked
explanation: An allow list permits only the items on the list and denies everything else. Malware never gets on the list, so it cannot run, which makes allow lists stronger than deny lists when the approved set is small.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: block one remote access tool that attackers abused in a recent incident
clues: every other installed application must keep working
the tool's name and file hash are known
staff install many different approved programs

answer.item: A deny list entry for the tool

appliesWhen: a few known items must be blocked while everything else is allowed
explanation: A deny list (block list) blocks only the items named on it and allows everything else. It fits when the bad item is known and the allowed software is too varied to list.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: restart the directory service during tonight's maintenance
clues: several applications sign users in through the service
one of those applications crashed the last time the service stopped
no one has recorded which systems rely on the service
appliesWhen: other systems rely on the component being changed
explanation: Dependencies are relationships where one service or application needs another to work. Mapping them before a restart shows which systems will be affected so they can be handled in the plan.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: keep an old inventory application running safely
clues: the vendor went out of business years ago
no security patches are available for the application
the warehouse still uses it every day

answer.item: Isolating the legacy application on its own network segment

appliesWhen: an old application that cannot be patched must keep running
explanation: Legacy applications are older programs that often lack vendor support and current security features. When one cannot be replaced or patched, isolating it limits what an attacker can reach through it.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: keep the production servers protected during a release freeze
clues: developers sometimes log in to production servers to test fixes
auditors flagged changes that were made outside the change process
only approved deployments should touch production

answer.item: Restricting direct access to the production environment

appliesWhen: certain actions must be blocked to protect systems outside the change process
explanation: Restricted activities are actions that are limited or prohibited to protect systems, such as direct changes to production. Restricting them forces changes through the approved process.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: close out a change that added a firewall between two network segments
clues: the network team uses the topology drawing to troubleshoot
the drawing still shows the old traffic path
a new engineer joins the team next week
appliesWhen: a change altered the network or system layout
explanation: Updating diagrams keeps drawings of networks and systems accurate after a change. Out-of-date diagrams lead to misunderstandings, misconfigurations, and security gaps.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: close out a change that replaced the VPN with a new remote access service
clues: the remote work instructions still tell users to start the old client
the help desk follows a written process that names the old service
the acceptable use rules mention the old VPN by name
appliesWhen: rules or written steps no longer match the systems after a change
explanation: Policies and procedures must be updated when a change makes them out of date. Otherwise staff follow the wrong guidance, which can create security gaps or compliance problems.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

need: track changes to the firewall configuration scripts
clues: three engineers edit the same scripts
last week no one could tell which edit broke a rule
the team must be able to return to any earlier copy of a script
appliesWhen: changes to files must be tracked with who made them and earlier versions kept
explanation: Version control records each change to a set of files, with when and by whom it was made, so any earlier version can be restored. It also gives an audit trail that helps spot unauthorized changes.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 3: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 3: Understanding Change Management’s Security Impact

task: making a change to the production firewall rules

steps.do: Submit a change request that names the owner and the reason
steps.done: submitted a change request that names the owner and the reason

steps.do: Perform an impact analysis of the change
steps.done: performed an impact analysis of the change

steps.do: Get approval from the change advisory board
steps.done: received approval from the change advisory board

steps.do: Make the change during the maintenance window with the backout plan ready
steps.done: made the change during the maintenance window

steps.do: Verify that the change works as intended
steps.done: verified that the change works as intended

explanation: A change starts as a documented request with an owner, is assessed with an impact analysis, and is approved by the change advisory board before any work. It is then made in the maintenance window with a backout plan ready, checked, and the documentation is updated so it matches the new state.
